notes.meaning: Jesus left Jerusalem in the evening to spend the night quietly on the Mount of Olives. He had no house in the city, so He withdrew outside the walls to rest and pray. Stepping away from the hostile leaders protected Him until the proper time for His public work.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Most modern scholars regard this story of the woman caught in adultery as a later addition that was not originally part of John's Gospel.

notes.meaning: At daybreak, Jesus returned to the temple courts where many people gathered around Him. He sat down as Jewish teachers usually did and began to instruct the crowd. He was eager to use every chance to share God's truth with those who sought Him.

Religious leaders interrupted Jesus by dragging forward a woman caught in adultery, which means being unfaithful to a marriage partner. They made her stand in front of the whole crowd to humiliate her and make an example of her. Their real aim was not to seek justice, but to set a trap for Jesus.

The leaders told Jesus that the woman was caught in the very act, leaving no doubt about her guilt. They pointed out that the law of Moses commanded that such an offender be put to death by stoning. Then they asked for His verdict, hoping to force Him to take a side.

The accusers tried to trap Jesus between two bad choices. If He ordered her execution, they could report Him to the Roman rulers who alone held the right to carry out death sentences; if He freed her, they would accuse Him of breaking God's law. Instead of answering right away, Jesus bent down and wrote in the dust with His finger, showing He would not be pulled into their scheme.

When the leaders kept pressing for an answer, Jesus straightened up and told whoever was without sin to throw the first stone. Under Jewish law, the witnesses had to throw the first stones during an execution, so He challenged their fitness to act as executioners. He showed that anyone eager to punish others must first look closely at their own heart.

After speaking, Jesus bent down again and continued writing on the ground. This quiet pause allowed the accusers to think about their own hidden sins away from His direct gaze. It gave them a chance to leave peacefully instead of arguing.

Troubled in their own consciences, the accusers walked away one by one, starting with the oldest men whose long lives held many sins. Soon none of the accusers were left, leaving the woman standing alone before Jesus and the crowd. God's truth has power to silence even the proudest critics.

Jesus straightened up and asked the woman where her accusers had gone, and if anyone remained to pass sentence on her. He did not ask because He was unaware, but to let her see that the immediate danger of death had passed. His gentle questions invited her to speak and trust Him.

The woman replied that no one was left to condemn her, and Jesus told her that He did not condemn her either. He did not act as a civil judge to order her death, nor did He excuse her wrongdoing. Instead, He offered her mercy and commanded her to leave her sinful lifestyle behind.

Jesus announced to the crowd that He is the light of the entire world. Just as the sun provides life and direction for the earth, Jesus provides spiritual life and moral guidance to all people. Whoever follows Him will not wander in the darkness of error and sin, but will have eternal life.

The Pharisees objected that Jesus was only speaking on His own behalf, which made His testimony invalid in court. In ordinary human affairs, a person could not serve as the only witness in their own favor. They used this legal rule to dismiss what He said about Himself.

Jesus replied that His testimony was completely true because He knew His heavenly origin and His destination. Unlike ordinary men, He came directly from God the Father and would soon return to Him. His critics were unable to judge Him fairly because they lacked spiritual knowledge.

Jesus told the leaders that they formed their opinions using outward appearances and worldly standards. He added that He was judging no one, meaning He did not come during His earthly ministry to condemn the world or act as a magistrate. His primary mission at that time was to bring salvation.

Jesus explained that whenever He does pass judgment, His verdict is reliable and true. He does not act as an isolated human judge, but stands in complete agreement with the Father who sent Him. Because God's authority is behind Him, His judgment cannot fail.

Jesus pointed to their own law of Moses, which required the testimony of two witnesses to confirm a matter. He explained that He had two divine witnesses: Himself and the Father who sent Him. The Father supported Jesus through the works and miracles He performed.

The Pharisees mocked Jesus by asking where this Father of His was, demanding to see Him in person. Jesus answered that their question showed how blind they were, since they knew neither Him nor His Father. The only way to truly know God is to know Jesus, who reveals Him.

Jesus taught these bold truths in the temple treasury, a public room where offerings were kept and priests were near. In spite of their anger, no one arrested Him because the exact time for His death had not yet arrived. God kept Him safe until His mission was complete.

Jesus warned the people that He was going away, and though they would later search for a savior in distress, they would die unforgiven in their sin. Because of their unbelief, they would never be able to enter heaven where He was going. Rejecting Christ leaves a person cut off from God.

Instead of taking the warning seriously, the Jewish leaders joked about what Jesus said. They asked if He planned to kill Himself, thinking that suicide would take Him to a dark place where they would never follow. Their hardened hearts caused them to mock God's offer of life.

Jesus explained the great contrast between His nature and theirs. They belonged to this lower, earthly world and lived by its corrupt desires, while He came from heaven and lived in pure fellowship with God. Earthly minds cannot understand heavenly realities on their own.

Jesus repeated that they would perish in their sins unless they believed that He is the promised Savior. By declaring that He is the one sent from God, He pointed to the only cure for human rebellion. Faith in Christ is the only way to be rescued from the penalty of sin.

The leaders asked Jesus who He claimed to be, speaking with scorn and irritation. Jesus told them that He was the very one He had declared Himself to be from the start, including the Light of the World and the Son sent by the Father. His claims had never changed, even though they refused to listen.

Jesus said He had many things to expose and judge about their wicked hearts, but He held back to focus on His commission. The Father who sent Him is entirely truthful, and Jesus faithfully told the world only what He received from Him. God will ultimately hold every person accountable to His truth.

The crowd still did not grasp that Jesus was speaking to them about God as His heavenly Father. Their stubborn prejudice kept them from seeing the clear meaning of His words. Unbelief blinds people to the simplest truths of God.

Jesus told them that after they had lifted Him up on the cross to die, they would finally realize who He truly is. His death, resurrection, and the coming judgment would show that He did nothing on His own, but spoke exactly what the Father taught Him. Even the hatred of His enemies ended up fulfilling God's plan.

Jesus explained that the Father who sent Him was always present with Him and never left Him alone. The Father remained with Him because Jesus always did what was pleasing in His sight, obeying Him perfectly. Believers find comfort in knowing that God stays close to those who trust and obey Him.

As Jesus spoke these serious words of warning and truth, many people in the crowd believed in Him. Even though the religious leaders opposed Him bitterly, His message touched open hearts and brought them to faith. God's word continues to bear fruit even in hostile surroundings.
